subtitle: Master rock lead techniques including power chord melodies, pentatonic applications, and aggressive phrasing.

introduction.title: Rock Lead Guitar: Power Meets Melody
introduction.text: Rock lead guitar combines the expressiveness of blues with the power and aggression that defines rock music. It's about making a statement. Rock solos need to cut through a powerful rhythm section. This requires precise technique, strong tone, and strategic note choices.

columns.title: Attitude and Aggression
columns.text: Key Elements: Strong attack, pentatonic foundation, power chord integration, controlled aggression

columns.title: Power and Precision
columns.text: Balance: Technical skill with emotional expression, complexity with memorability, power with musicality

cards.title: Power Chord Melodies
cards.description: Using power chord shapes to create melodic lead lines

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Combine single notes with power chord shapes for thick, powerful melodies

fields.label: Key Players
fields.value: AC/DC, Black Sabbath, early Metallica

fields.label: Practice
fields.value: Play pentatonic scales using power chord fingerings where possible

cards.title: Pentatonic Mastery
cards.description: Advanced application of minor and major pentatonic scales

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Five positions, string skipping, sequences, connecting patterns

fields.label: Key Players
fields.value: Jimmy Page, Slash, Kirk Hammett, Zakk Wylde

fields.label: Practice
fields.value: Learn all five pentatonic positions and practice connecting them smoothly

cards.title: Aggressive Phrasing
cards.description: Rhythmic attack and note emphasis that creates rock attitude

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Hard pick attack, palm muting, rhythmic accents, staccato playing

fields.label: Key Players
fields.value: Angus Young, Tony Iommi, James Hetfield lead lines

fields.label: Practice
fields.value: Practice same licks with different attack intensities and rhythmic feels

cards.title: High-Gain Techniques
cards.description: Using distortion and overdrive to create sustain and harmonic content

fields.label: Application
fields.value: Pinch harmonics, controlled feedback, sustain management

fields.label: Key Players
fields.value: Dimebag Darrell, Randy Rhoads, Eddie Van Halen

fields.label: Practice
fields.value: Practice with clean tone first, then add gain to hear the difference

cards.title: Minor Pentatonic
cards.description: Foundation for most rock lead playing, works over minor and major progressions

cards.title: Major Pentatonic
cards.description: Over major chord progressions, Southern rock, classic rock ballads

cards.title: Natural Minor
cards.description: Metal, heavy rock, dramatic passages, minor key songs

cards.title: Mixolydian Mode
cards.description: Over dominant 7th chords, Southern rock, blues-rock fusion

cards.title: I-bVII-IV Progression
cards.description: Emphasize power and resolution, use power chord melodies

fields.label: Example
fields.value: A-G-D (in A)

fields.label: Best Scales
fields.value: A minor pentatonic, A Mixolydian

fields.label: Songs
fields.value: "Sweet Child O' Mine", "TNT", many rock anthems

cards.title: i-bVI-bVII Progression
cards.description: Use minor scales, emphasize emotional bending and vibrato

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Am-F-G (in Am)

fields.label: Best Scales
fields.value: A natural minor, A minor pentatonic

fields.label: Songs
fields.value: "Stairway to Heaven" verses, "Nothing Else Matters"

cards.title: I-V-vi-IV Progression
cards.description: Target chord tones, use major pentatonic over major chords

fields.label: Example
fields.value: G-D-Em-C

fields.label: Best Scales
fields.value: G major pentatonic, E minor pentatonic

fields.label: Songs
fields.value: "Let It Be", "Don't Stop Believin'", many ballads

cards.title: Modal Rock Progressions
cards.description: Use specific modes for each section, create modal color

fields.label: Example
fields.value: Various modes over static bass

fields.label: Best Scales
fields.value: Modal scales matching the progression

fields.label: Songs
fields.value: Tool, Dream Theater, progressive rock

sections.title: Rock Lead Styles Through the Decades

cards.title: Classic Rock
cards.description: Pentatonic-based, blues influence, moderate gain

fields.label: Key Players
fields.value: Jimmy Page, David Gilmour, Jimi Hendrix, Eric Clapton

fields.label: Techniques
fields.value: String bending, vibrato, feedback control, blues-rock fusion

fields.label: Equipment
fields.value: Marshall amps, Les Pauls, Strats, moderate overdrive

cards.title: Heavy Metal
cards.description: High gain, fast playing, darker harmony, power chords

fields.label: Key Players
fields.value: Tony Iommi, Randy Rhoads, Yngwie Malmsteen, Dimebag Darrell

fields.label: Techniques
fields.value: Palm muting, alternate picking, sweep picking, harmonic minor scales

fields.label: Equipment
fields.value: High-gain amps, humbucker pickups, effects pedals

cards.title: Hard Rock
cards.description: Aggressive but melodic, anthemic solos, strong hooks

fields.label: Key Players
fields.value: Angus Young, Slash, Joe Perry, Eddie Van Halen

fields.label: Techniques
fields.value: Power chord melodies, pentatonic mastery, tapping, aggressive phrasing

fields.label: Equipment
fields.value: Marshall stacks, Gibson guitars, moderate to high gain

cards.title: Grunge/Alternative
cards.description: Raw tone, simple but effective, emotional expression

fields.label: Key Players
fields.value: Jerry Cantrell, Kim Thayil, Billy Corgan, Kurt Cobain

fields.label: Techniques
fields.value: Power chords, simple solos, heavy use of effects, drop tunings

fields.label: Equipment
fields.value: Distortion pedals, unconventional guitars, raw production

cards.title: Power Chord Melodies
cards.description: Use power chord shapes (root + 5th) to create thick, powerful melodic lines that cut through heavy mixes. Common in AC/DC, Black Sabbath, and early metal.

cards.title: Octave Displacement
cards.description: Play the same note in different octaves using power chord fingerings for dramatic effect and fuller sound. Creates powerful, anthemic quality.

cards.title: Single Note + Power Chord
cards.description: Alternate between single-note lines and power chord punctuation for dynamic contrast. Builds intensity and creates rhythmic interest.

cards.title: "Sweet Child O' Mine" - Guns N' Roses (Slash)
cards.description: G minor pentatonic with chromatic passing tones, wide vibrato, aggressive bending

fields.label: Structure
fields.value: Builds from simple melody to complex runs, excellent use of space and phrasing

cards.title: "Eruption" - Van Halen (Eddie Van Halen)
cards.description: Two-hand tapping, tremolo picking, harmonics, revolutionary approach

fields.label: Impact
fields.value: Redefined what rock lead guitar could be, introduced new techniques to mainstream

cards.title: "Highway to Hell" - AC/DC (Angus Young)
cards.description: Pure pentatonic mastery, aggressive attack, simple but effective phrasing

fields.label: Lesson
fields.value: Proves that technical complexity isn't required for memorable, powerful solos

cards.title: "Crazy Train" - Ozzy Osbourne (Randy Rhoads)
cards.description: Classical influence, harmonic minor scales, precise alternate picking

fields.label: Innovation
fields.value: Brought classical music theory and technique to heavy metal

cards.title: Gain Structure
cards.description: Matching gain levels to rock subgenre.
items: Classic Rock: Moderate overdrive, tube amp distortion
Hard Rock: More gain, tighter bass response
Metal: High gain, noise gate, precision
Balance: Enough gain for sustain, not so much you lose clarity

cards.title: EQ Considerations
cards.description: Shaping your lead tone to cut through the mix.
items: Mids: Cut through the mix, don't scoop too much
Treble: Clarity and bite, but avoid harshness
Bass: Tight and controlled, avoid muddiness
Presence: Helps solos sit on top of the mix

cards.title: Essential Effects
cards.description: Core effects for rock lead guitar tone.

practiceSection.title: Rock Lead Practice Routine
items: Pentatonic Mastery: Master all five positions of minor and major pentatonic. Practice connecting patterns smoothly.
Rhythm Integration: Practice lead lines that incorporate rhythmic elements. Learn to play lead that supports the song's groove.
Solo Learning: Learn classic rock solos note-for-note. Analyze phrasing, tone, and how they fit the song.
Jamming: Jam over rock backing tracks. Focus on creating memorable, singable melodies with attitude.
